title: The danger of the modern gospel
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: A watered-down understanding of Christianity has left too many young men living on spiritual vibes. To him, God's sacred nature means very little; he prefers a mix-and-match faith,…
body: A watered-down understanding of Christianity has left too many young men living on spiritual vibes. To him, God's sacred nature means very little; he prefers a mix-and-match faith, half in the world, half in the church, completely confused about what true consecration actually looks like.

He flows effortlessly with the culture, and the moment his conscience is poked, his shields go straight up: "Where is it in Scripture? Show me where it's written!" To him, anyone living a dedicated, consecrated life is just over-righteous or an extremist.
He knows nothing about surrendering to God's will or presenting his life as a living sacrifice. He isn't seeking God's glory; he's just using faith as a stage to package himself and chase clout.
He knows nothing about the God who warned that trials and tribulations are part of the walk. In his mind, God is just a shortcut to getting insanely rich and satisfying the hidden idols of his heart.

He has no clue that the God who lifts is the same God who refines His own through the dark valleys of life. He's been fed a designer gospel that paints Christianity as pure luxury without trial. But at the end of the day, the root problem is simple: he relies entirely on Sunday motivational speeches because he never opens the Word for himself.

title: The earthly man and the spiritual man
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: To be earthly is to be sensual, to be heavenly is to be spiritual.
body:
To be earthly is to be sensual,
to be heavenly is to be spiritual.

The earthly mind seeks that which is earthly,
and the spiritual mind seeks that which is eternal.

The earthly man's actions are sensibly sponsored,
and the spiritual man's actions are biblically sponsored.

One seeks earthly treasure,
while the other seeks heavenly enrichment through the use of earthly resources.

The earthly man is not rapture-conscious,
but the heavenly man is earnestly awaiting the second coming of Christ.

The earthly man seeks earthly plaudits,
whereas the spiritual man seeks a heavenly recognition.

title: Place is no barrier
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: I do not always need to shout; my silent whispers are enough to strike a chord in His heart.
body: I do not always need to shout; my silent whispers are enough to strike a chord in His heart.
My prayers do not move Him; they only show my willingness to receive the help He is already willing to render.
Therefore, whatever limitation keeps me from praying aloud will never restrict my communion.
Place is no barrier. Deep within my heart, I can make my willingness known, sincerely laying bare the state of my soul to my Lover.

title: The false climax
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Yes! There's a climax. It is worth celebrating, but it is far short of the destination. It comes in our daily pursuit of God, as well as our…
body:
Yes! There's a climax.
It is worth celebrating, but it is far short of the destination.
It comes in our daily pursuit of God,
as well as our journey in life,
and in all we do.

When we are celebrated by men,
when the applause of men resounds and never stops.

When we are set on a new colt that has never been ridden upon,
as Jesus was hailed "Hosanna" as He passed through the midst of the people,
He was called a King already; what then did He need anymore?

But it's a FALSE CLIMAX!
There was more to that; there was a greater glory that awaited Him.
This climax is an enticement from the devil; never fall for it!

There's still more!
There's a greater glory than the now!
There are more depths to reach,
there are more heights to attain.
Keep on going.

title: That all men be saved
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: I have a burning passion beneath my chest. It hasn't consumed me yet, but it is eating me up, gradually. It is an ache to see the young…
body: I have a burning passion beneath my chest. It hasn't consumed me yet, but it is eating me up, gradually. It is an ache to see the young and the old coming to give their lives to Jesus, because they do not deserve to be where the tyrant devil has destined them to be.

The burden in my heart is one that, if fulfilled in my lifetime, I wouldn't have a single pinch of regret in the grave. Riches, fame, honours: they are all fleeting. But there is a passion of love raging within my heart to see men become like Christ.

I remember weeping during one of my last days in university, at the last sermon I preached. Seeing three souls born again right there, I broke down. I said, "Lord, I'm done. Lord, I am not leaving in vain. Lord, I am pleased. I just hope You are pleased with me."

I have been driven by this desire: that I may know Him and become like Him, and that others may also know Him and become like Him. Four years ago, this became the goal of my life. It is what I have vowed to live for.

I have prayed, and I am still praying: Lord, for every ounce of fleeting breath I draw above this dusty ground, give me the grace to labour. Not seeking plaudits. Not seeking applause. But to live pleasing in Your sight for the one single cause for which You died: that all men be saved.

title: Humanity does not come first
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Humanity does not come first. The One who created humanity comes first.
body: Humanity does not come first. The One who created humanity comes first.

This is because no one truly knows how, or has the natural ability, to be correctly humane on their own. True religion teaches a person to put others before themselves and empowers you to do the same. It is not a problem of religion itself; rather, it is a problem of finding the right religion, because the true faith puts others first and loves others genuinely.

title: Do not pitch your tent with Sodom
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Do not pitch your tent with Sodom and expect your heart to be set on what is heavenly. Except the heavenly call bids you to go and preach…
body: Do not pitch your tent with Sodom and expect your heart to be set on what is heavenly. Except the heavenly call bids you to go and preach at Nineveh, it is not wisdom to dwell in the seat of the scornful, for from such the Lord withdraws His blessedness.

To be true, you must fill your heart continually with truth. To continue to be new, that which is of the New Creation must be the habitation of your heart. Do not sow the seeds of corruption and expect to reap the fruit of righteousness. What you sow into your heart is what you will get as character.
Even the little foxes spoil the vine, so it is better to avoid all than to play with a little that is in no way less than the big.

title: Sold out for His cause
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Some of us dare not kick against the pricks; we cannot dare to waver from the heavenly vision, as our security is tied to our obedience. We were…
body: Some of us dare not kick against the pricks; we cannot dare to waver from the heavenly vision, as our security is tied to our obedience. We were not just casually saved; we know and realise how far we had gone, and the great damage the devil would have wreaked upon our souls.

Because of this, we cannot help but pour out our lives further and further at His feet. We are sold out only for His cause because we recognise the depth of His saving grace. We do not even deserve to be alive because of the devil's plots, but He came through to save us; therefore, He is worthy of us giving back what He took upon Himself to rescue. He owns this life, and He deserves the full use of it.

We cannot beat our chests. All our goodness is tied to the benevolence of His mercy and the deep work of His grace. We cannot despise others because we know we were once blind just like them; we can only kneel in prayer for lost souls.

title: Give me the old-time religion
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: The claim of modernism is that the plague of our fathers was intellectual inaccessibility and educational deficiency, while hyper-intellectualism and excessive reliance on reason have become the plague…
body: The claim of modernism is that the plague of our fathers was intellectual inaccessibility and educational deficiency, while hyper-intellectualism and excessive reliance on reason have become the plague of our generation.
The latter generation contends that our fathers were entangled in the web of religion, blindly following its tenets, which limited their achievements.

We have embraced what we call modern Christianity, which we have intellectually mapped out, yet we struggle to reach even a fraction of the spiritual depth they attained. We have become so intellectually proud that acts of simple faith seem foolish to us, as we demand rationality in all matters.
If adopting old traditions in a new manner fails to produce results comparable to those achieved by the original methods, then it is the height of wisdom to return to the old ways.
I do not desire modern Christianity with diminished impact, power, presence and holiness of life, accompanied by increased boastfulness.
Give me the old-time religion.

title: It is good for me to draw near to God
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: I have travelled to many isles, journeyed across different land masses, I have toured the beautiful streets in the city of thought, I have sojourned through the diverse…
body:
I have travelled to many isles,
journeyed across different land masses,
I have toured the beautiful streets in the city of thought,
I have sojourned through the diverse facets of earthly terrain,
yet I have found no rest in any.

Upon a thorough examination of all I could vividly behold,
I conducted a careful weighing on a balance,
yet I could deduce nothing but voidness and anxiousness,
apart from sadness and temporary relief,
which only leads men to perdition.
I could find rest in none.

Finally, I came to a halt in my search.
I reached a climax of decision,
having journeyed through the narrowness of all paths.
There I stepped and ceased searching,
for it is there alone that rest resides on all sides.
To Him alone must my heart draw,
for in Him alone there is peace and rest.
(Psalm 73:28)

title: Hardship or compromise
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: It's not every time you will have an equal or better alternative when standing for righteousness. There are times you have to settle for the worst when standing…
body: It's not every time you will have an equal or better alternative when standing for righteousness. There are times you have to settle for the worst when standing for truth. Sometimes hardship is the only alternative to compromise.

Most of the time, the way of righteousness is a hard route, but we have the hope of commendation from the Father and the assurance of formidable integrity among men. We also have grace as an advantage to go through it all.

title: Kept in the Lord by the Lord
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: There is often misunderstanding around some teachings concerning the finished work of Christ, especially regarding the Old Man, the New Man and the flesh.
body: There is often misunderstanding around some teachings concerning the finished work of Christ, especially regarding the Old Man, the New Man and the flesh.

The Old Man is the sinful nature that every person is born with. For everyone who is truly born again, the Old Man was crucified with Christ. It was crucified once and for all at the cross, and we are to reckon it dead (Romans 6:11).
The New Man is the new nature we receive when we are saved, the very life of Christ dwelling in us (Ephesians 4:24; Colossians 3:10).
The flesh is not the Old Man. Rather, it is the believer operating in self-reliance, apart from the Holy Spirit, expressing itself through the body, mind and will (Romans 8:8; Galatians 5:16–17).

The key to victorious Christian living is not merely having the new life, but submitting it to the guidance of the Holy Spirit. Only the Spirit knows the mind of Christ and can strengthen us to live His life (John 14:26; Philippians 2:13).

The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of counsel and might (Isaiah 11:2). He does not only reveal God's will to us; He also supplies the strength to carry it out (Acts 1:8). Temptation will still come, but we have no hope of standing unless we are both submitted to the Holy Spirit and strengthened by Him.
Many times, we stumble not because we do not know God's will, but because we attempt to obey it in our own strength (Galatians 2:20).
To live triumphantly, we must depend on the Holy Spirit for both direction and power. This is how Jesus lived, and this is how we are called to live as believers (Luke 4:1; John 5:19).

title: Free from men's expectations
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: The consciousness of men's expectations concerning our lives makes us live a life full of fear, comparison and unnecessary pressure, and most times this is truly our mindset.
body: The consciousness of men's expectations concerning our lives makes us live a life full of fear, comparison and unnecessary pressure, and most times this is truly our mindset.
Take a step at a time, follow the Master's instructions, walk in purpose, and focus on God's demands and expectations. This is how we ought to live.

title: On speaking in tongues
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: There is a widely held assumption in many Christian gatherings that until the leader in prayer or worship bursts out in tongues, the Holy Spirit has not yet…
body: There is a widely held assumption in many Christian gatherings that until the leader in prayer or worship bursts out in tongues, the Holy Spirit has not yet come. This idea, though often sincere, finds no solid foundation in Scripture and must be examined carefully in the light of God's Word.

Likewise, the practice of speaking in tongues from the pulpit while addressing a congregation calls for serious biblical correction. For some, it has become a tradition; for others, an imitation of well-known Christian figures; and in certain cases, a substitute for the quiet labour of being grounded in Scripture. Yet none of these are safe guides for the church of Christ. The only safe guide is the written Word of God.

The Scriptures speak with clarity on this matter. In 1 Corinthians 14:5, the apostle Paul teaches that prophecy, speech that is understood, is greater than tongues unless interpretation is provided, because God's chief concern in the assembly is the edification of the church.

Again, in 1 Corinthians 14:28, Paul gives a direct command: "If there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church." This instruction leaves no room for disorder or self-expression that does not profit the hearers.

Paul then reveals the spirit behind these commands in 1 Corinthians 14:19, where he declares that he would rather speak five intelligible words in the church than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue. The value of speech in public worship is not measured by how spiritual it sounds, but by how clearly it communicates truth and builds up God's people.

From these passages, one truth stands out plainly: the Holy Spirit never works against understanding. He is not the author of confusion, nor does He delight in displays that draw attention to the speaker while leaving the congregation unedified. Where there is no understanding, there is no instruction; and where there is no instruction, there is no growth.

It is therefore time for the church to return to the simplicity and order of apostolic Christianity. Public worship must be governed by love for God's people, reverence for God's Word and submission to God's commands. Emotional fervour, however sincere, must never be allowed to replace biblical obedience.

The true mark of the Spirit's presence is not noise, but fruit; not disorder, but edification; not imitation, but conformity to Scripture. Let us therefore examine our practices honestly, lay aside what cannot be defended from the Word of God, and seek to worship Him in spirit and in truth.

title: When the curtain closes
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: When the light is out, when the curtain closes and the light fades, what will the next scene be?
body: When the light is out, when the curtain closes and the light fades, what will the next scene be?
When the curtain is drawn on a man's life here on earth, where will the destination be?
A smile comes to my face when I hear people say, "I own my life." Really? You think you do? A life that can be taken without your consent, and you think you own it?
You do not know what will happen tomorrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour that appears for a little time and then vanishes away.

title: What is your priority?
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Time neither begs nor forgives. Childhood fades away swiftly, while adulthood rushes forth like an erupting volcano. Old age slips away like water from the palm. Time remains…
body: Time neither begs nor forgives. Childhood fades away swiftly, while adulthood rushes forth like an erupting volcano. Old age slips away like water from the palm. Time remains relentless, unaffected by a person's engagement or disdain.
At the outset, let us focus on what truly holds significance in the end.
May we avoid the regret of realising our misguided choices, by embracing wisdom and foresight early on.
In no time, everything you see will cease to exist, so seek what is eternal.

title: Just a servant on pilgrimage
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Six years ago, a decision to follow Jesus was made. Four years ago, the terms of agreement were completed. Two years ago, the pilgrimage began. And now, here…
body:
Six years ago, a decision to follow Jesus was made.
Four years ago, the terms of agreement were completed.
Two years ago, the pilgrimage began.
And now, here is a leap forward on this sojourn.

Let them fade, all that is worldly.
Let them fade, all that is earthly.
Let them fade, all that is not eternal.
Keep me steadfastly pressing on to the Home not made with hands.

Teach me, Lord, to always lean on Your breast,
to live solely by faith,
to live only by Your Word,
and to live daily by prayer.

This is a new year!
A leap forward in this sojourn.

title: Dare to walk the heavenly path
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Dare to walk the heavenly path of destiny, but prepare your heart for obstacles, as you may face imprisonment like Joseph or persecution like David.
body: Dare to walk the heavenly path of destiny, but prepare your heart for obstacles, as you may face imprisonment like Joseph or persecution like David.
However, remember that if you follow God just as you are led, you will have the Alpha and Omega holding up your hands all through, till you enter your divine inheritance.

title: He calls me His son
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: I have once been neglected! I have once been despised! I have once been rejected! But He alone received and remoulded me!
body:
I have once been neglected!
I have once been despised!
I have once been rejected!
But He alone received and remoulded me!

He calls me His son!
I call Him my Father!
For He endows me with all things,
and He gave to me His name
to bring under subjection the forces of darkness!

He taught my hands to war,
and my legs to battle!
I do not have to be afraid,
for He's with me everywhere I go!

Who is He?
Jesus, the Man of Calvary.

title: Give me a friend so divine
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Give me a friend so divine, a friend forged and refined in the furnace of Your love, salted and melted under the heat of Your brokenness, cleansed and…
body:
Give me a friend so divine,
a friend forged and refined in the furnace of Your love,
salted and melted under the heat of Your brokenness,
cleansed and crushed at Calvary.

Grant me a friend, solely from You,
a friend whose heart bears the imprint of Your burning love for immortal souls,
single-minded and fixed on the mark of the cross,
dead to sin and alive only to You.

title: Forge us, O Lord
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: There is a battle, a battle at the gates. There is a war, a war at the garrison. The enemy has infiltrated the land of our Father.
body:
There is a battle,
a battle at the gates.
There is a war,
a war at the garrison.
The enemy has infiltrated the land of our Father.

Forge us, O Lord,
as the battle axe of righteousness.
Mould us, O Lord,
into Your instrument of war.

Teach us to pray, to live,
to fight with valour.
Guide us in the art of war,
as we defend our sacred soil.

title: Guard the loins of your heart
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Our hearts are fragile; they tend to sway away from what is true and pure, even the crucified heart.
body: Our hearts are fragile; they tend to sway away from what is true and pure, even the crucified heart.

Guard the loins of your heart, streamline the content you feed on, and be intentional about the direction of your heart. Do not let it be void of that which is good for a second; fill it and keep filling it with what is right.

Be intentional about your thoughts.
Be resolute about holiness.
Be determined regarding purity.
Set a watch over the door of your heart.
Again, guard the loins of your heart.

title: More than a confession
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Good confessions amount to mere professions that only give temporary hope and comfort without prayer.
body: Good confessions amount to mere professions that only give temporary hope and comfort without prayer.
God does nothing without an answer to prayer. "Ask," He said. "Pray," He instructed. "This kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting" was the word of the Master to the perplexed disciples.

title: Sons of thunder in the pulpit
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: We need more Boanerges, sons of thunder, in the pulpit. We need men who will flash forth the law of God like livid lightning and arouse the consciences…
body: We need more Boanerges, sons of thunder, in the pulpit. We need men who will flash forth the law of God like livid lightning and arouse the consciences of men. We need more Puritanism in the pulpit.
Away with this milk-and-water preaching of a love of Christ that has no holiness or moral discrimination in it.
Away with preaching a love of God that is not angry with sinners every day.
Away with preaching a Christ not crucified for sin.

title: How strong is your foundation?
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: The moments that demand the practice of our faith probe and make plain the solidity of our foundation in the faith we profess.
body: The moments that demand the practice of our faith probe and make plain the solidity of our foundation in the faith we profess.
How strong is your foundation?
How firm are your convictions?

title: A memo to Christian writers
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Dear Christian writer, there's a fire burning in your bosom to change your world. It is clear that you want to be a voice; I have no doubt…
body: Dear Christian writer, there's a fire burning in your bosom to change your world. It is clear that you want to be a voice; I have no doubt that you have a great desire to impact everyone around you. But I have some notable claims concerning your zeal.
My claims won't be words resting on human philosophy, but on that old Word of Life. The old path is that which is forever right and never untrue.
Never write because you want to write. Never write because you feel like writing. Don't write because others are writing.
Before you write, ask yourself this significant question: do you have a message for the world around you?

Prophets, brethren and apostles in time past did not speak or write, or even come forth, until they had a message for the world around them. The justification for their writing was beyond passion, emotion, sensation and the burning zeal within them; beyond this, they waited patiently to receive from Him who has the right message for the wrong world.
This is a proven claim in the Word, and this is the kind of message that affects and transforms. Elijah, Micaiah, Paul, Jude, James and many more are proofs of it.
Get a message from Him for your world before you write. Shalom!

title: The perfect choice
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Beautiful, but not qualified! Handsome, but not worthy!
body:
Beautiful, but not qualified!
Handsome, but not worthy!
These are the alarm bells that the Father sounds earnestly in the hearing of His beloved sons and daughters.

Perfection resides in Him and with Him. Worthiness isn't a result of what the eyes can behold, but goes far beyond the comprehension of the eyes, deeper into the spirit realm, without ambiguity or emotional entanglement.
Here is where no quarrel resides. It is not one-sided, not won by persuasiveness, but settled with full surety.
His will may not appeal to your pleasure and specifications, but it's the best you can and will ever have.

title: You cannot bow out now
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: You cannot bow out now! Oh no, you can't. The Father has laboured so much on you for a cause, not to bow out.
body:
You cannot bow out now!
Oh no, you can't.
The Father has laboured so much on you for a cause, not to bow out.

Distracted?
With the fear of the unknown?
Intimidation and persecution?
The glory of the world keeps flashing?
Ostentation all around?

Remember Calvary,
why He went there.
Only for the essence of the cross should we live.
Keep looking at the Man of Calvary.
Keep on holding on.
He will bear you safe to the destination.

title: A simple cry for help
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: If only we all knew how small we are as vessels carrying His will.
body: If only we all knew how small we are as vessels carrying His will.

If we are able to see how feeble and incapable we are, we will see the need for enlargement and help in carrying out His will. The short and simple prayer, "Lord, help me," will mean a whole lot to us.
Weary? Tired? Weak? In weakness His strength is made perfect; He helps the weak. Those who are healthy need no doctor, but the sick do.
A simple cry of "Lord, help me," prayed in all sincerity, the Father cannot despise.

title: What the thick clouds bring
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: There are things the thick clouds birth: great things and wonderful ones.
body: There are things the thick clouds birth: great things and wonderful ones.

Though the thick clouds may disrupt the day, the water drops they bring forth water the ground and the seeds, and cause them to bring forth fruit in bountiful folds. They also give water for the survival of men, and afterwards the sky becomes clearer.
The thickness of the cloud may look unpleasant, but its benefits pay far more than its disruption.

title: It was written
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Before I could breathe the first breath, it was written, written concerning me, what would become of me.
body:
Before I could breathe the first breath, it was written,
written concerning me, what would become of me.

Has it not been said?
At a young stage of my life,
was it not evident?

I thought of hiding, but instead I drew closer than usual.
As I moved in this direction, there the pull was,
drawing me closer to the reality.
The farther I go, the closer I become.

Can I really run from this?
But it dawned on me that rejecting Him is rejecting life,
and neglecting His will is a choice of destruction.
As I turned to run the race in His chosen path,
I saw greater things than what I had seen.

Are there not treasures up there which He has prepared,
that even earthly glory cannot withstand?
The best He has prepared, and that I have chosen.

The year just past has been the best yet.
Indeed the Lord has helped me.

title: To the place of the cross
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: I will turn my back, run far away, sever all ties, all connections.
body:
I will turn my back,
run far away,
sever all ties,
all connections.

I will turn, but not from the Lord.
I will run far away from the world to the place of the cross,
the only place where newness broke forth and where victory lies.

I will sever all ties with the world and all it entails.
No connection with the world anymore:
I am crucified to the world, and the world to me.

title: The change that starts within
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: As much as science has helped us, it can also become one of the tools with which the god of this age blinds people's eyes. It still baffles…
body: As much as science has helped us, it can also become one of the tools with which the god of this age blinds people's eyes. It still baffles me how great some professors and scientists are, how vast in knowledge, and yet they find the Father unsearchable, though He is nearer than our thoughts can comprehend.

Principles of life, tested, tried and proven, only model people's lives externally, and so produce hypocrisy. All this cannot work. The real change in man starts from the inside and then flows outward, and the activator of this change is the Word, giving life by the Spirit. Only this can transform a man completely.

title: Who are you?
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: I know you are beautiful, and indeed you are skilful, in fact one of the best in what you do. Speak of being intelligent: of course you can't…
body: I know you are beautiful, and indeed you are skilful, in fact one of the best in what you do. Speak of being intelligent: of course you can't be discarded, probably one of the best in your department, your level or your field. I have read your portfolio; you have a beautiful one. And I haven't forgotten you have a fat bank account too. These are lovely things that speak about you.
But do you think all these clearly define who you are? What if all were taken away, as happened to Job? Who will you be then? What shall we use to describe you?

When it all ends here on earth, I hope it has not also ended in eternity. A true life cannot be defined without the person of Jesus; He is the one who brings meaning to life and an essence to existence. We are not living as men whose bus stop is here, but as those who live for a glorious home not made with hands, whose builder is God Himself.

I am not a definition of what the world offers or presents, but of divine essence. I have been ordained to be an expression of God, a definition of His beauty, a representation of His unchanging love. Nothing changes Him; as He was in ages past, so He is now.
When beauty, money, position, fame and possessions are all gone, who will you be then? Only Jesus gives an everlasting definition that no disaster can tamper with.

title: Dear visionary
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Dear visionary, I know you have seen plainly what His purpose for your life is, but never be eager or rush to manifest, so that you won't rush…
body: Dear visionary, I know you have seen plainly what His purpose for your life is, but never be eager or rush to manifest, so that you won't rush in.

You are too young to become history. Sit with the Lord and learn of Him. Let all excesses be purged, let the flesh and its desires be nailed to the cross, let self and its centredness be taken away, let the death of the cross work in you.

You will do yourself much good by doing this. Listen, and take note of every bit of His instruction. Learn to sit, hear and obey. With this, our patriarchs of faith were able to bring down God's perfect will in their generation and end their journey of faith well.

title: Fear clips your wings
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: Fear cripples a man; it clips his wings. It blindfolds a man from seeing the light in the darkness. It blurs his vision from seeing the provision made…
body: Fear cripples a man; it clips his wings. It blindfolds a man from seeing the light in the darkness. It blurs his vision from seeing the provision made available for his journey.
Everyone has fear; some have simply overcome theirs. True victory over fear reaches every area of life, so that they no longer fear even death itself, and this victory resides only in God.
Only the Holy Spirit gives such victory. You can open your heart today to the Spirit of sonship, of power and of a sound mind. He is waiting for you.

title: Be led
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: On the platform of "Emi lokan" (I am the next to have this, to become this and that), as much as urgency is required, don't lose your birthright.…
body: On the platform of "Emi lokan" (I am the next to have this, to become this and that), as much as urgency is required, don't lose your birthright. Watch out, so as not to be sifted.
You can never be more accurate in analysis and strategy than the Spirit of God.
Be led! I repeat, be led!

title: The main cast
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: The summary of a man's life is a storyline. Each day counts in the telling; it doesn't have to start well, but it must end well.
body: The summary of a man's life is a storyline. Each day counts in the telling; it doesn't have to start well, but it must end well.
You are the main cast; God is the Scriptwriter and the Director of the play.

At some point you may feel the need to deviate from what He who holds the real script has written. But I'd like to tell you that it will only make shipwreck of all you're meant to portray, and in the end you will not pass on the message the Director desires. What a wasted investment it would be!

Follow the Director's instruction, and His alone, and be sure the instruction is not from the crowd or from how you think it should go. The heroes of faith are waiting to watch the outcome of the beautiful story.

title: His choices are the best
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: We stray away just because we can't trust His decisions for our lives.
body: We stray away just because we can't trust His decisions for our lives.
We often forget that He has travelled before time began; He has gone through all the pages and chapters of our lives before they are presented to us.

We often forget His great love for humanity: that He would go to the extent of the sacrifice on the cross at Calvary, the cross of pain, agony and anguish. Will He now choose what is bad for the man He suffered and died for?
Always remember that His choices are the best. You have to trust Him. You need to trust Him. He loves you more than you love yourself.

title: We are new
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: From Calvary breaks forth our newness; at Golgotha was our old nature put to death. We are no more who we were once called; indeed the old man…
body:
He died; we are dead,
for our sins and the old nature
on Him were imputed.
He's alive; we are alive,
for He overcame and arose anew.

We are free!
We are new!

title: The darkest night is before the dawn
author: Godwin Ayorinde Olaewe
excerpt: I know there are many people out there struggling, striving, working harder to find a way out of one situation or another that they are stuck in. Some…
body: I know there are many people out there struggling, striving, working harder to find a way out of one situation or another that they are stuck in. Some situations came as a result of personal errors, family issues or challenges, and yet, relentlessly, they keep fighting to catch a glimpse of light at the other end of the tunnel.
I would like to encourage you never to relent. The light you have been fighting to glimpse is almost within reach. You won't only have a glimpse; you'll walk in it, live in it and rejoice in it.
The dark days are only for a season. They do not last long for those who never relent in pursuing the light at the end of the tunnel.
Remember: the darkest night is always before the dawn. The light comes with the dawn; the darkest night never lasts.
